text:
**No Intent-project management state reaches a user-facing surface.** (hv ruling, 2026-08-15, direct: _"NEVER EVER put Intent project management state like ST or WP numbers or ACs etc into output from Intent. Intent as a tool cannot expose its internal project management state in its output. Some other project doesn't care about an AC or a WP or even a test that is in the Intent project itself."_) **Scope is OUTPUT, not source**: no ST id, WP number, AC/AT id, decision number or Intent test name may appear in anything the shipped binaries emit -- errors, remedies, refusals, help and usage text, `doctor` findings, GraphQL error messages, daemon banners, or any rendered view of a consumer's project. Comments and Intent's own test fixtures are out of scope; they are never seen by a consumer. **The finding this AC is written from is that the leak is STRUCTURAL rather than incidental** (vc, measured 2026-08-15): `transitions.rs` carries an `owed_by: "WP-06"` field, `dispatch.rs` defaults an entry owner to `"WP-06"`, and `render.rs` renders both into remedies a consumer reads -- so a field in the model is DESIGNED to carry Intent's roadmap into another project's terminal. Six emitted sites measured: `render.rs:300` (remedy names WP-06), `render.rs:324` (error names ST0056 and the owning node), `render.rs:745` (remedy's worked example is `ST0056/03`), `intentd/main.rs:10` (startup banner), `graphql.rs:128` (client-visible resolver error), `ingest.rs:279` (scaffolding refusal). **The replacement statement is the consumer-meaningful one and is strictly more useful: say what is unavailable and what to do instead, never who owes it or under which work package** -- "not available in this build" is actionable, "owed by WP-06" is an invitation to read a roadmap the reader has no access to. Worked examples in remedies use a neutral id, never Intent's own. **CORRECTION 2026-08-15, same day, before anyone built to it: the six-site measurement above is the SMALL half.** `dispatch.rs:41` compiles `surface/dispatch-table.json` into the binary with `include_str!`, and that file carries **121 Intent PM identifiers** (25 `WP-06`, 11 `WP-05`, ten distinct ST ids, and AC ids including this thread's own) as parity prose describing v2 behaviour. So the carrier is **embedded DATA, not source string literals**, and it is 20x the size of the literal surface. Found by dc measuring something else entirely -- AC-11.3's `INTENT_HOME` question -- which is the second time today a real finding arrived from an unrelated lane. **What is NOT asserted, because it is not measured: whether those 121 are ever EMITTED.** The `owner` field demonstrably is (`render.rs:324`); the parity prose may never reach a surface, in which case it is out of hv's stated scope, which is output. **It is one renderer change away from being in scope, and it is what any auditor will see first.** **MEASURED 2026-08-15, closing that gap the same hour rather than leaving it for whoever implements: of the 121, exactly EIGHT are emitted, and all eight are `owner_wp`. **[MEASUREMENT DECAYED IN OUR FAVOUR, RE-MEASURED 2026-08-15 (vc, on cc's report, verified rather than taken): it is now ZERO emitted, not eight.** `owner_wp` has NO read site anywhere in the workspace -- `dispatch.rs:104` declares it and `dispatch.rs:220` defaults it, and the `owner()` function and the `render.rs` site this clause traced are gone; `intentd/main.rs` and `graphql.rs` are both fixed, each leaving a comment recording what it used to read. **The count above is kept because a criterion that quietly restates its own numbers cannot be audited, and because the direction of decay is the point: a stale measurement reads as current evidence whether it decayed in our favour or against us.** Fifth instance of this class in this contract, all mine.**]

**EXTENDED 2026-08-20 (hv, direct, on seeing thread ids in code again; contracted by vc). THE SCOPE LINE ABOVE READS `OUTPUT, NOT SOURCE`, AND THAT MISSES THE THIRD CASE: INTENT WRITES FILES INTO OTHER PEOPLE'S REPOSITORIES.** A template copied by `st new`, a hook installed into `.git/hooks/`, a skill or subagent installed into `.claude/`, and the rule library served to a consumer's agent are none of them binary output, and none of them are comments a consumer never sees -- they are the opposite, artefacts whose whole purpose is to be read inside another project. **This criterion's own title says user-facing SURFACE and its body said OUTPUT; the body was the narrower of the two and the payload fell through the difference.** Measured 2026-08-20 (vc, at `92ed515c`): **80 Intent PM references across 25 files of installed payload** -- 30 in `lib/templates/`, 24 in shipped skills and subagents, 23 in plugin shell source, 3 in the rules library.

**THE DISCRIMINATOR IS CITATION VERSUS FORMAT EXAMPLE, and it is mechanical rather than a judgement per site.** `intent st show ST0042` in a skill teaches syntax and costs a consumer nothing -- the id is a placeholder that happens to be four digits. **A CITATION points into a tracker the reader cannot open.** `plugins/claude/rules/_schema/critic-contract.md:52` reads _"Rejected alternative documented in `intent/st/ST0034/design.md` D5"_, naming a path that exists in no consumer's project **and in this one no longer either**, since `intent/st/` has held ST0046, ST0056 and ST0057 alone since `e7f00e65`. **A citation that has gone dangling inside its own repository is the clearest possible statement that the reference was never for the reader.** Citations go; examples stay, re-based on `ST0000` where convenient. **The instance every user meets is `lib/templates/prj/st/ST####/acceptance.md:30`, carrying _"Exemption (ST0048)"_ -- so every steel thread created in every project is stamped with an Intent thread number.**
